bib.title: A Constructive Prediction of the Generalization Error Across Scales

read.skipped: Appendix D extrapolation grids (Figs 16-21) are numeric subplot labels only; skimmed, not itemised.

question: What is the functional form relating generalization error to both model size and dataset size, and can it extrapolate from small to large scale?
hypothesis: A simple joint form (sum of a data power law, a model power law and an irreducible term, with a random-guess envelope) approximates the error landscape and extrapolates.
contributions: A joint functional form of the generalization error landscape, dependent on both data and model size, with few interpretable degrees of freedom
Direct and complete specification (via the scaling policy) of the model configuration attaining said error across model and dataset sizes
Highly accurate approximation of error measurements across model and data scales on different models, datasets and tasks
Highly accurate error prediction from small to large model and data

method.summary: Train fixed-hyperparameter model families at a grid of width scales and data fractions on 6 vision and 3 language datasets, observe saturating power laws in each axis, propose eps_hat(m,n)=eps0*(e~/(e~-i*eta)) with e~=a n^-alpha + b m^-beta + c_inf, fit it by least squares on relative error, and test by 10-fold cross-validation and by extrapolating from small (m,n) to larger configurations.
method.task: error-landscape fitting and extrapolation for image classification and word-level language modeling

datasets.name: ImageNet
datasets.preprocessing: uniform class subsampling by a constant ratio; test set untouched

datasets.name: DTD / Aircraft / UCF101
datasets.split: 2^-k N, 0<=k<=5; Rebuffi et al. 2017 train/val/test split
datasets.source: Cimpoi 2014; Maji 2013; Soomro 2012 (UCF101 converted to one image per video via Bilen 2016)
datasets.preprocessing: versions collated and resized by Rebuffi et al. 2017

datasets.name: PTB
datasets.preprocessing: random sentence sampling to a fraction of total words

other.scaling: width 4^-k M; CIFAR10 -3<=k<=4, CIFAR100 -2<=k<=4; depth scaling probe on CIFAR10 (D=8..128, W=1..128)

training.objective: image classification cross-entropy / word-level language modeling cross-entropy (error = top-1 error or test cross-entropy loss)
training.optimizer: SGD momentum 0.9 for ResNet/WRN/AWD-LSTM; Adam for Transformer-XL; VGG and DenseNet with both SGD and Adam (default Adam hyperparameters)
training.lr: 0.1 (SGD vision); 1e-3 (Adam, VGG/DenseNet); LM rates not stated in paper (official implementations)
training.lr_schedule: step x0.1: ImageNet after epochs 30 and 60; other vision after 80, 120, and 160 epochs; VGG SGD same; DenseNet SGD after 150 and 225 epochs

other.hyperparameters: held fixed across all scales, no tuning at large scale

inference.samples: extrapolation fit repeated 10 times (main text) or 100 times (Appendix D) with different random initialisations of theta; training run seeds per configuration not stated

metrics.name: divergence delta
metrics.definition: (eps_hat(m,n;theta) - eps(m,n)) / eps(m,n), reported as mean mu and std sigma over configurations

eval.protocol: least squares on relative divergence; 10-fold CV over all (m,n) per dataset, +-1 std over folds; extrapolation fits on all points with m<=mi, n<=nj and tests on all larger points

results.quote: under 5% when extrapolating from a slimmed-down model (1/16 of the parameters) on a fraction of the training data (1/8 of the examples)

results.claim: WikiText-103 extrapolation from M/16, N/8 has mean divergence 0.5% (std 1.7%).

results.claim: 10-fold cross-validated fit quality is worst-case mean under 1% and std under 5% across datasets, with at most 6 free parameters against 42-49 configurations.
The form holds across VGG, DenseNet and WRN with SGD and Adam on CIFAR100 with mean divergence under 1%.

results.table: Table 2a, row ImageNet, column alpha (beta 0.61, b 0.76, c_inf 3.63, eta 18.50)

results.claim: Extrapolation fails when fit points sit near the random-guess plateau or number fewer than the free parameters of theta.
results.setup: Appendix D extrapolation grids, all datasets
results.note: Authors say at least two measurements per scaling dimension and no fewer than |theta| in total are needed

results.claim: Compute-optimal model-to-data ratio under FLOPs proportional to m*n is given by b*(beta/alpha)*n^alpha/m^beta = 1.
results.setup: Minimise m*n subject to constant error contour c = n^-alpha + b m^-beta; assumes constant epoch budget

limits: Hyperparameters held constant across scales; no hyperparameter scaling policy shown (authors' conjecture only)

Transition from random-guess level is modelled by a convenience envelope; random-guess levels for small-model and small-data cases assumed identical, which fits worse for imbalanced language modeling (Fig 15)
Overfitting with larger models seen in one dataset (UCF101, Fig 12); form does not capture it
Extrapolation ill-posed near the random-guess plateau or with fewer points than parameters

No theory for the form; word-level LSTM/Transformer-XL and CNNs of 2019, up to 100M-word corpora and ImageNet; no large-scale subword LLM pretraining; compute/FLOPs trade-off is a derivation, not measured
Training seeds, hardware and compute are not stated

code.snippet: eps_hat(m,n) = eps0 * (~eps / (~eps - i*eta)); eps_inf = eps0 * c_inf / eta; a=1 WLOG; theta = {alpha, beta, b, c_inf, eta}
